channel.description: English audio from AI-skiftet: two-host dialogues based on selected essays, plus the weekly and monthly AI round-ups.

item.title: August 2026 - The Month in AI: The labs hit the brakes, the capital hit the gas
item.description: August 2026 was the month when the industry's two forces pulled hard in opposite directions. Safety incidents made the labs brake their own models while capital poured into infrastructure faster than ever. In between, the EU transparency rules took effect in earnest, the Nordics became one of the world's most sought-after places to build AI - and the question of what all this AI actually delivers got its first uncomfortable numbers.

item.title: Week 35 - The Week in AI: The chip giant, the ownership changes and the machines
item.description: Five lines shaped the week of August 24-30, 2026: Nvidia set the pace in both directions, ownership changes reached Norwegian robotics and Nordic language models, agents left the screen and took hold of physical machines, labour-market effects got numbers while the measurement base turned out to be thin - and the rulebooks diverged while the technology tested them.

item.title: Week 34 - The Week in AI: The school year, the safety limits and the power
item.description: Five lines shaped the week of August 17-23, 2026: the new school year made children and teenagers the front line of regulation, safety work became visible, the burden of proof on AI cut both ways, the Nordics became a construction site while public opinion cooled - and capital tied itself together more tightly as the thresholds fell.

item.title: Week 33 - The Week in AI: Arendal week, capital and the burden of proof
item.description: Five lines shaped the week of August 10-16, 2026: Norwegian AI policy gathered in Arendal, costs kept redrawing the hardware, labelling and safety limits left the level of principle, the burden of proof on AI's benefits caught up - and the quantum field delivered three results in a single week.

item.title: The Race, the Megawatts and the Last Piece of Software
item.description: A conversation tying together the three latest essays: Hassabis' proposal for governing frontier AI, the Nordic grid queues, and what happens to business models when the agent becomes the way in.

item.title: Week 32 - The Week in AI: Calibration, cost hunting and Norwegian power
item.description: Four lines shaped the week of August 4-10, 2026: safety moved from theory into day-to-day operations, costs began to steer the hardware, the Nordics stepped forward as the engine room of the AI build-out, and regulation and the labour market kept falling out of step.

item.title: When the Ladder Was Pulled Up
item.description: On AI, global development and whether the industrial and service ladders are being pulled up for the countries that still need them most.

item.title: The Breach of Trust
item.description: On the night Fable 5 and Mythos 5 went dark, and why the question shifts from which model is best to which model cannot be taken away.

item.title: AGI and what it actually means
item.description: On AGI as a capacity profile, uncertainty and why preparation matters before definitions settle.

item.title: The Civilisational Shift
item.description: On why AI, robotics, energy and automation together amount to a civilisational shift.

item.title: AI is not just a tool
item.description: On why AI should be treated as a system shift for work, administration and competitiveness.

item.title: After work
item.description: On meaning, identity and institutions in a society where less human wage work is needed.

item.title: The missing consistency condition
item.description: On the contradiction between AI job forecasts, Swedish tech founders' policy wish list and the labour market their own products transform.
